written_before: any of the code below existed, and before anything was measured
question: Make the shares the audit commits to be the shares MP-SPDZ consumes.

the_gap.policy_audit.share: Shamir VSS over group.order, degree t, t+1 coefficient commitments
the_gap.qomm_transport.roles.split: additive over the integers with 40 bits of slack per share
the_gap.consequence: a maker can commit to policy P, prove P in band, and deal P' to the nodes; every check passes

route_taken.name: Shamir inputs over the ed25519 group order
route_taken.why: BINDING.md section 2 measured the matched field at 1.00x rounds, 2.00x traffic, 1.07x wall. Once the MPC field is the group order, a Shamir share IS a scalar, so the VSS the audit already publishes can be the input.
route_taken.circuit_change: secret_input() becomes sum(lambda_p * get_input_from(p)) over all n parties, with public Lagrange coefficients at zero. Interpolating from all n rather than t+1 keeps the input count and the circuit shape identical.

rejected_alternative.name: additive VSS over l, one commitment per share
rejected_alternative.why_not: publishes n points per value instead of t+1, so 7/3 = 2.33x the commitment bytes at n=7, t=2 --- and it would need no circuit change, which is the only thing it wins

predictions.rounds: unchanged. A public constant times a secret input is local.
predictions.traffic: unchanged against the same field. The coefficients are public.
predictions.input_count: unchanged: n reads per value, same as today.
predictions.field: must be the group order, 253 bits. The 128-bit default cannot hold a scalar.
predictions.verify_share_cost: t+1 = 3 point exponentiations plus one commitment per share, so about 5 scalar multiplications. At 37.3 us each on host-c, about 0.19 ms per share per field.
predictions.whole_policy_at_n7_t2: 10 fields x 7 nodes = 70 share checks, about 13 ms, plus the range proofs the audit already pays
predictions.wire: unchanged from the audit today: t+1 = 3 points per field
predictions.risk_1: MP-SPDZ may refuse a 253-bit prime for malicious Shamir, or need -F 253 to round up to a supported width. BINDING.md says -F at compile and -P at run time is the supported path and measured it, so this is expected to work and is the thing to check first.
predictions.risk_2: the Lagrange coefficients are computed mod l in Python and must be emitted as MP-SPDZ constants of the same field. A mismatch shows up as a wrong answer rather than an error.
predictions.risk_3: the existing input files are integer additive shares. Both formats have to coexist or every harness that writes inputs changes at once.

what_would_falsify_this: the circuit answering wrongly at the matched field with Lagrange coefficients, or the round count moving

outcome.written_after: the chain ran end to end against MP-SPDZ over the group order
outcome.traffic: predicted unchanged at the same field; measured 1.9994x against the default field, which is the element width 16 -> 32 bytes and nothing else. That is the field's cost, not the chain's, and section 2 had already measured it at 2.00x.
outcome.input_count: predicted unchanged; measured 86 values either way. Correct.
outcome.verify_share_cost: predicted 0.19 ms per share per field; measured 0.167 ms. Correct to within the estimate's own precision.
outcome.risk_1_field: did not fire. -F 253 at compile and -P at run time worked first time, as BINDING.md section 2.1 said it would.
outcome.risk_2_coefficients: did not fire, and it was the one to watch --- a mismatch would have been a wrong answer rather than an error. Guarded by running both arms on the same market and requiring the same non-trivial answer, (99970, 1). A run whose reference says 'no eligible maker' verifies trivially and proves nothing; the first attempt did exactly that and was discarded.
outcome.risk_3_two_formats: fired, and was resolved rather than worked around. Both dealings coexist behind one flag, and the order of the input stream stayed in the one place that already knew it --- `build_inputs` gained a hook instead of the binding module gaining a copy of the ordering. A copy is what caused the original gap.
outcome.not_predicted: that `finish_reference` had to be split out of the generator's main(). Two callers now need the sentinel and packing rules, and a second copy of 'no eligible maker' would have been the same class of bug one level down.
